messages.content: Hi Liu. I am planning a trip from Beijing to Lhasa on the high-speed rail soon. Have you ever taken that route?
Actually, I have taken it twice since last year. It is a long journey, but the scenery along the way is amazing. You will see the Qilian Mountains and the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau.
That sounds wonderful. How much do the tickets cost now? I remember they were cheaper in the past.
Prices have risen a bit since last year. A second-class seat usually costs around 1000 yuan, but prices depend on how far you book in advance. If you book early, you might get a better deal.
I see. Do I need to make a reservation online? Can I just buy a ticket at the station?
You should book online because tickets sell out very quickly. Although you can try the station counter, it is often crowded. I recommend using the official railway app.
Okay, I will check the app tonight. Speaking of safety, are there any risks on this train?
It is generally safe, but you must prepare for altitude changes. The air is thinner in Lhasa, so many people feel dizzy. It is wise to take some medicine beforehand.
Good advice. What about the food? I am worried about finding good meals on the train.

The train car has a restaurant selling noodles and dumplings. However, I think you should bring some snacks like dried beef because the menu is limited. You can also buy local snacks like yak butter tea if you want.
I like the idea of bringing snacks. By the way, can you tell me the rule for using 'a' versus 'the' when I describe the food I bring?
Good question. Use 'a' for new things like 'a bottle of water' and 'the' for specific ones like 'the bottle in my hand'. I usually pack a thermos for hot tea on the trip.
That is very helpful. What if I get sick due to the altitude? Is there a hospital near the stops?
There are medical stations in major cities like Xining and Golmud along the way. If you feel unwell, the train staff can help you call them. It is better to stay calm and rest.
I feel much better now. Do you think I should stop in Xining for a night before going to Lhasa?
Yes, I strongly suggest it. You can adjust to the altitude slowly. In Xining, you can try local Tibetan food and visit the Great Mosque of Xining. It makes the whole trip more enjoyable.
Perfect. I will add Xining to my itinerary. Thanks for all the information, Liu.
You are welcome. Just remember to book your tickets soon. The spring season is busy, so do not wait too long.

messages.content: Hello, Lao Zhang! It is wonderful to see your shop on West Lake Old Street. I am Jing Hua, and I am looking for some good tea leaves to send to my friends in Wenzhou. Do you have any recommendations for spring tea?

Hello Jing Hua! Welcome to my little shop. Yes, we have the best Longjing tea from this year. The leaves are fresh, and the flavor is very smooth. Since you are sending gifts, we can also put them in nice bamboo boxes for your friends. Have you been to West Lake often?

Yes, I have visited West Lake many times since I moved here five years ago. Actually, I remember the first time I tried tea here; it was amazing. But today, I want to buy a little more than usual because I want to surprise my family.

That is a very kind thought. To be honest, buying tea for family is a great tradition. The price is a little high today, but the quality is worth it. If you wait until next month, the prices might be lower. Would you like to try a small sample first?

Sure, I would love to try a sample. Oh, wait, I have a question. You just said, 'If you wait until next month, the prices might be lower.' How do you conjugate 'to be' in the future tense? Like, is it 'will be' or 'will are'?
Good question! It is 'will be'. We use 'will be' for future states. For example, 'The prices will be lower next month.' Now, back to the tea, do you like the taste of the sample?
It tastes very good, actually. Although it is a bit expensive, I think the quality is excellent. I also need to pack these gifts carefully. Do you have any special bags for sending tea?

Yes, we have beautiful silk bags and wooden boxes. My father used to make wooden boxes in the old days, and I still use his designs. They are very strong and look elegant. Which style do you prefer, something traditional or something modern?
I think something traditional would be better. My friends will love the wooden boxes. By the way, if I buy two boxes, can you give me a discount?

If you buy two boxes, I can give you a small discount. Actually, buying in bulk is common here. But first, let me show you the packaging. We can write your friends' addresses on the outside so they know where it comes from. Is that important to you?
Yes, that is very important. My friends live far away, so they need to know it is from Hangzhou. Thank you for your help, Lao Zhang. I think I will buy two wooden boxes now.

Excellent choice! I will pack them right away. The tea is ready, and the boxes are beautiful. I hope your friends enjoy the gift. In addition to the tea, maybe you can bring some photos of West Lake next time you visit?
That is a great idea! I will definitely bring some photos. I have taken many pictures since I started living here. Thank you again for the wonderful tea and the packaging.
You are welcome, Jing Hua. It is my pleasure to serve you. Enjoy your trip back to your family, and send them my regards. Come back anytime you need more tea!

messages.content: Hey Lin, this night market in Guilin is amazing. Have you tried the roasted sweet potatoes here?
Actually, yes! I bought a few earlier. They are soft and very sweet, especially when the weather is hot like this. The vendors usually sell them near the entrance to the market.
I've been wanting to try them since I arrived in Guilin last week, but there are so many choices.

That's true. You have options like grilled squid, rice noodles, and various meat skewers. If you don't want spicy food, avoid the chili powder on the side. Have you considered going to the food street near the Li River?
I guess I could, but I don't speak Chinese well enough to order. Can you give me a list of words for ordering food?
Good question! You can use simple words like "I would like" or "How much is this?" to start. For example, "I would like two bowls of rice noodles" works well.
Thanks, that helps. What about asking for less oil? Is there a specific phrase for that?
Yes, you can say "less oil, please." In Guangxi, dishes like stir-fried pork might be oily, so it's helpful to ask. By the way, have you seen the colorful lanterns hanging above the stalls?
Yes, they are very bright. It reminds me of the festivals in Chongqing, but here it feels more relaxed.
Exactly. Guilin has a slower pace compared to big cities. If you come back next month, you might want to try the local rice wine with some duck. It goes very well with the food.
I'd love to try the duck. Do you think it is expensive? I am on a budget.
Not really. A plate of braised duck is quite reasonable, maybe around 30 yuan. You can share it with a friend if you want. Are you planning to visit Yangshuo after tonight?
Yes, I have a ticket for the boat trip tomorrow. I hope the weather stays nice.
It usually is. Although it is summer, the river breeze keeps it cool. Just remember to bring your camera to take pictures of the karst mountains. They look incredible from the water.

messages.content: Hello! I'm Wei, a traveler from Chengdu. The mist here near Mount Qingcheng is amazing. It feels like we are in a painting since the rain started this morning.
Yes, the humidity makes the air very thick. Actually, it has been raining here for over a week, so the forest is wet and green. Are you planning to hike up the mountain soon?
I would love to, but I'm worried. If the rain stops, I can try the path to the panda habitat. However, if it rains heavily, I guess I will just stay here.
That is a smart plan. The path to the panda habitat is steep, so we should wait for dry weather. I have been waiting for the clouds to clear since yesterday.
Speaking of waiting, can you explain why we use 'have been waiting' here instead of 'was waiting'? I find the present perfect tense confusing when talking about the past.
Good question! We use it because the action started in the past and is still important or connected to now. For example, I have lived here for five years, which means I still live here.
Ah, I see. So it emphasizes the connection to the present. What if I say, 'I was waiting for the bus since morning'? Is that wrong?

Yes, that would be incorrect. You should say, 'I have been waiting for the bus since morning,' because you are likely still waiting or just finished waiting. Using 'was' would imply the action is completely over.
Okay, that makes sense. Let's talk about the weather again. Although the humidity is high here, I think it is better than the dry air in Beijing. What do you think?
To be honest, many people prefer the dry weather in Beijing, but I like the cool mist here. It feels refreshing after a long day. Have you ever visited Beijing before?
Yes, I visited last winter. The Great Wall was impressive, but the air was so dry. In addition to the weather, the food here is much better than in the city.

messages.content: Hi, I am Zhang Ling. It is a nice spring morning here in Xiao Jianghuai. I saw your notice board about the community cleanup next week. Do you think we should start early in the morning to avoid the heat?

That is wonderful! Your dedication is inspiring. Since you have been coming for so long, you probably know the best spots where trash tends to accumulate. Do you remember how last summer the situation was different?
Actually, last summer was very different. While we were walking, I noticed that more people were throwing trash because of the festival. But this year, I guess the community spirit is stronger.
I agree. It is good to see that the spirit of the community has grown. We also plan to organize a small tea tasting after the cleanup. We can use some local jasmine tea from nearby gardens.
Jasmine tea would be perfect! I have never tried the one made in our local area. By the way, can you tell me the rule for using 'a' versus 'the' in sentences like this?

Ah, I see! So in my sentence about the festival, I should say 'a festival' because it was the first time I mentioned it? And if I talk about the festival again, I use 'the'?

Yes, offering dumplings would definitely encourage more volunteers! Many families would like to bring their children if there is food. It makes the event much more welcoming.

You are very welcome, Zhang Ling. Your enthusiasm is the key to our success. Let us meet at the center gate at nine o'clock next Sunday. See you then!

messages.content: Hello, Mr. Zhang. It is great to meet you at the entrance of Stone Forest Park. I have been coming here since I retired from teaching in Kunming. The morning air is so fresh.

Yes, I am. Actually, I have been waiting for the perfect weather to explore the stone formations. But I am worried about bringing enough water. The trails can be hot even in the morning.

You are right to be careful. The stone forest gets very hot quickly. You should pack at least two large bottles of purified water. Also, make sure you do not leave any trash behind so the wildlife stays safe.
That is a good point. I usually pack snacks like rice cakes or dried fruit. Do you think I can see any wildlife here, like monkeys or birds?
Yes, there are many birds in the trees along the path. Sometimes you might see langurs hiding in the rocks if you are quiet. But remember, do not shout so they can be undisturbed.

Actually, I use it quite a bit. For example, I say 'The sun IS hot' or 'The wind IS cool.' We use the present simple form for current conditions. It is very different from saying what happened yesterday.
Ah, I see. So I should say 'The sun is hot' now. But what if I talk about yesterday? Do I change the word 'is' to something else, like 'was'?

That is quite common during busy mornings. Many patients come to the hospital in the winter to get checked for colds or flu. Since you have a headache and dry eyes, I suspect you might need some eye drops or maybe some herbal tea to help you relax.
Herbal tea? That sounds nice. But I don't know which kind to buy. Can you give me a list of words for describing my symptoms so I can order medicine correctly?

Good question! Here are some key words you can use: 'dizzy', 'nauseous', 'fever', 'cough', and 'fatigue'. For example, you can say, 'I have been feeling dizzy since yesterday.' This helps me understand your condition better.
Oh, I understand now. So I should say 'I have been feeling dizzy since yesterday.' That makes sense. By the way, do you think I should take a train home or go by taxi?

Since you are feeling dizzy, I would recommend taking a taxi or calling a relative to pick you up, rather than driving yourself. The metro can be crowded, and you might get dizzy on the platform. How about we start the examination now?
Okay, I am ready. If I take a taxi, will it be expensive in Nanjing? I have a limited budget this month.

Taxis in Nanjing are reasonably priced, but if you go during rush hour, they might be a bit more expensive. If you have time, you could also wait for the metro later when it is less crowded. For now, let's focus on your health.
Alright. I guess I will just take the taxi to my office in Xuanwu Lake district. Thank you, Doctor.
You are welcome, Ming Wei. I will prescribe some eye drops and maybe some traditional Chinese medicine tea for your fatigue. Remember, taking a break is important. Take care of yourself!

That is very wise. In TCM, we often balance diet and exercise first. If you have been feeling stiff for a long time, seeing a doctor in Jinjiang or Huaxi could help. Actually, I think you should book an appointment before trying acupuncture yourself.
I have been doing some research online, but I am confused about the grammar I am using. I said 'I have been feeling stiff'. Can you explain why we use 'have been' here instead of 'was'?

That sounds like a great idea. Do you think I could rent a small space there? I would like to arrange the frames properly.

Oh, I have heard about that tea shop. It opened last year. I think I will visit it next week. While I am there, I might buy some fresh ink. What do you think?

messages.content: Hello, Doctor Wang. I am Chen Hao. I have been feeling very tired lately since last month, and I think I need a physical exam before my trip to Suzhou next week.

Hello, Chen Hao. It is good that you are being proactive about your health. Yes, a full check-up is a very important idea. At our clinic in Nanjing, we can schedule this easily. Would you like to book a morning slot today or perhaps tomorrow morning?
A morning slot tomorrow would be perfect. I usually work until late in the afternoon, so I have no energy for the clinic then. What tests do we need to do?

For a standard physical, we will check your blood pressure, listen to your heart and lungs, and do a basic blood test. Since you mentioned fatigue, we will also check your blood sugar and cholesterol levels. These are common issues in our city these days.
Okay, that sounds reasonable. I am a bit worried about my blood pressure because my uncle had high blood pressure. I guess I should take some medicine to lower it before the trip, right?

It is smart to be concerned, but please do not start taking medicine without a proper diagnosis first. Actually, many people have normal blood pressure at home but it spikes slightly when they arrive at the hospital, which we call white coat syndrome. We will measure it carefully here.

I see. So I shouldn't assume anything based on family history alone. By the way, I heard there are many good doctors here who can tell the difference between modern medicine and traditional Chinese medicine. Which one should I choose for my fatigue?

That is a great question. Actually, for general fatigue and mild blood pressure issues, a combination of both can be very effective. Many patients here choose acupuncture from our traditional department alongside the blood tests we do here. It helps relax the body.

That makes sense. I think I will try the traditional therapy if it helps with my sleep, but I want to know the exact numbers from the blood test first. Can you explain why we use the word 'the' in 'the blood pressure' but sometimes 'a' in 'a blood test'?

For example, 'I need to do a blood test' means any test, but 'the results of the blood test' refers to the specific paper in your hand.

Ah, I understand now. So 'a' is for new things and 'the' is for things we already know about. I feel much clearer now. Okay, I will come tomorrow at 9 AM. Is there anything else I should prepare before coming here?

Yes, please do not eat breakfast before you come here this morning, as it can affect your blood sugar results. You can bring a warm cup of tea to drink after the exam. In addition, bring your ID card and your insurance card if you have one.
Got it, I will come on an empty stomach. Thank you, Doctor Wang. I really appreciate your advice. I feel less anxious now that I know the plan.

You are very welcome, Chen Hao. Taking care of your health is the best decision you can make. I hope your trip to Suzhou is wonderful and that you feel refreshed by the time you return. See you tomorrow at 9 AM.

messages.content: Hey, I've been thinking about a weekend getaway. Since I've lived in Chengdu for five years, I know the food here is amazing, but I want to try something new in Sichuan province. Have you ever been to Leshan?

Oh, absolutely! I went there last spring. We took a train from Chengdu to Leshan, which took about two hours. The Grand Buddha statue is huge, and there are so many local snacks in the old town. Actually, the morning market near the river is my favorite spot.
That sounds great. I'm planning to visit next month. If I book my ticket early, will it be cheaper? I don't want to miss out on the spicy hot pot or the famous duck necks.

Yes, booking in advance is usually much cheaper. You can also avoid the huge crowds during the holiday. For food, you should try the cold tofu with chili oil; it's delicious and not too spicy. I guess you'd love it if you like bold flavors.
I definitely like bold flavors. But I'm worried about the crowds. What if it rains on Saturday? Should I still go out?
Don't worry too much. Even if it rains, the ancient town has many covered walkways. You can sit in a small tea house and drink a cup of jasmine tea while watching people walk by. It's quite peaceful.

That sounds relaxing. By the way, I've been trying to improve my English, but sometimes I get confused with verb tenses. For example, I say 'I am planning to go' but I heard you say 'I went'. How do you conjugate 'to be' in past tense?
Good question! We use 'was' or 'were' depending on the subject. For instance, 'I was planning to go' means the plan happened before now. It helps us describe past actions clearly.
Oh, I see. So 'I was planning' is different from 'I am planning'. Got it. Anyway, since I might stay for two days, do you recommend staying near the Yellow Dragon Cave or the Grand Buddha?

If you want to see the cave, stay near the Yellow Dragon Cave area; it's closer to the park. But if you prefer food and shopping, the Grand Buddha area is better because there are more restaurants. You can easily walk to both places if you don't mind a bit of walking.
Perfect. I think I'll stay near the Grand Buddha. What about the train back? Is there a direct line to Chengdu?
Yes, there is a direct train. It runs every hour during the day, so you won't have to wait long. You can also take a taxi if you're tired. How much do you usually spend on travel?
I try to keep it under 300 yuan. Is that enough for a round trip?
That should be enough. The train ticket is around 25 yuan one way, and a taxi is much cheaper than in big cities. You can also buy local snacks for lunch. It's a great deal.
Thanks for your advice! I feel much more confident now. I'll book the train soon. Let's meet up next month to explore Leshan together!
Sounds like a plan! I'll message you next week to confirm the date. Enjoy your trip, and don't forget to try the duck necks!

messages.content: Hi Qiang. I finally bought an old apartment in the Tang Paradise Community here in Xi'an. I'm really excited, but I have a lot of work ahead of me.
That's great news, Xiao Fang! Congrats on the new home. How is the renovation going? Have you started choosing new furniture yet?

Yes, I have. I was looking at some wooden tables and chairs. But there's a problem; the construction work next door has been going on for weeks. It's been terrible since morning, and I can't concentrate on picking out items.

Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. Noise is a real headache in our old neighborhoods. Did you check if the building management can stop the work for a while? Or maybe you could wear earplugs while you are making your final decisions.

Maybe, but I also need to check the safety standards of the new sofa I found. I want to make sure the materials are safe for my family. Can you give me a list of words for describing materials and safety features?

Good idea. Words like 'eco-friendly', 'non-toxic', and 'fire-resistant' are very important. For example, you should ask the seller if the fabric is 'flame-retardant' or if the wood is 'formaldehyde-free'. Safety is always the top priority.
Thanks. I guess I will write those down. If I find a sofa that is safe, I will buy it immediately. Do you think I should also look at a dining table for the living room?

Actually, a dining table usually goes in the dining room, not the living room, unless your space is very small. Since your apartment is in a historic district, maybe choose a traditional Chinese table with a nice lacquer finish to match the style.
That sounds wonderful. I love traditional furniture. I hope I can finish the renovation before the next hot summer. What do you usually do when it's too noisy to work?

I usually step outside and buy some fresh fruit and tea at a nearby market, then wait for the noise to stop. Sometimes, I listen to classical Chinese music to calm myself down while I plan the next steps.
That is a good strategy. I might try that. By the way, I've been trying to improve my English by talking to you. It helps a lot. Thank you for your advice.
You're very welcome. It is my pleasure to help. Just keep practicing, and soon you will feel much more confident. Let me know if you need any more tips on renovation or English!

I guess I prefer stability. I have been studying computer science for three years now, so I want a place where I can grow steadily.

That sounds great. I've been hiking since last year, so I'm not a beginner. What should I bring? I think I need a lot of water.

You're right about the water. Actually, it's better to bring a thermos of hot tea too, because the temperature drops quickly at higher altitudes. Also, don't forget your windbreaker, although it's autumn, the mountain wind can be very cold.
I guess I'll pack a thermos and a jacket. By the way, do you think I should bring my tent or just a sleeping bag in case we stay overnight?

I checked the app, and it says there might be a slight chance of rain. Should we change our plan to the indoor museum in Lijiang Old Town instead?
That's a good idea if the rain gets heavy. Although the museum is indoors, it's quite far from my house. If the rain is just a drizzle, we can still go to the mountain and just wear our raincoats.
To be honest, I prefer the hike. Let's hope the rain stays away. If it rains, we can just meet at the cafe in the square later.
Sounds like a solid plan. We can grab some jasmine tea at the square and decide then. Let me know if you need any help buying supplies at the market before we leave!

messages.content: Hello, I am Xiao Fang. I have been feeling very tired since Monday morning. I think I should make an appointment with a doctor to check my health.
Hi Xiao Fang, welcome to our clinic in Hangzhou. I am sorry to hear you feel tired. Yes, it is a good idea to see a doctor. Have you had this headache for a long time or just lately?
It started last week. I have been working overtime at the office near Xixi Wetland Park. Although I sleep a lot, I cannot get enough rest.

Working too much often causes tiredness, especially in busy cities like Hangzhou. Let me check the schedule for you. We have Dr. Zhang who specializes in general health. She will be seeing patients after 10 AM tomorrow.
Tomorrow is fine for me. Can I book an appointment for 11 AM? I am not sure if I will be able to come earlier.
Sure, 11 AM works well. By the way, what symptoms are you experiencing besides the headache? Are you coughing or having fever?
No fever, but sometimes I feel dizzy when I stand up quickly. My colleague told me that I might be dehydrated. Is that a serious problem?

It is better to check it out. Dehydration can happen if you forget to drink water during long work hours. In addition, the rainy weather in Hangzhou might make you feel unwell. I will note your symptoms for Dr. Zhang.
Thank you. One more thing, if the doctor says I need to rest more, what should I do about my work?

Good question! Actually, you can tell your manager that you are not feeling well. For example, you could say, 'I have been working hard, but I need to take a day off.' Then you can focus on your health.
That sounds reasonable. I guess I will try to use that sentence. How do I conjugate 'have been' if I want to say I worked yesterday?
I see, you just need to change 'have been' to 'was' or 'worked' for past actions. For instance, you could say, 'I worked yesterday.' Now, shall I book that 11 AM slot for you?
Yes, please book it for me. What time does the clinic usually close?
We close at 5 PM on weekdays. If you need to wait for the result, you can come back later or call us next time. Your appointment is confirmed for tomorrow at 11 AM. Do you need any medicine now?
No, not today. I will drink more water and rest tonight. Thank you for your help, receptionist.
You are welcome, Xiao Fang. Take care of yourself! Remember, if you feel better after drinking water, that is a good sign. See you tomorrow for your check-up.

messages.content: Doctor Li, I've been feeling really tired these days. It's been raining since last week, and the damp weather in Yuexiu District makes me feel even worse. I've been working late at the office in Tianhe since Monday, and now my head hurts a lot.
Hello Huang. It is very common to feel this way during the rainy season. Please sit down. Your symptoms suggest you are damp and Qi is deficient. Have you been drinking warm water?
Actually, I drink more coffee instead. I usually buy an Americano at the shop near my building because I think it helps me stay awake. But now I feel exhausted by 3 PM.

Coffee might wake you up for a short time, but it can make your body more damp and heavy. In traditional medicine, we prefer to drink warm ginger tea or a simple herbal soup to warm the stomach. Would you like to try a bag of Chrysanthemum tea today?
Chrysanthemum tea? I have heard of it, but I don't know how it tastes. Is it bitter like dark beer? Also, what kind of soup do you recommend for my stomach?

Chrysanthemum tea is quite sweet and floral, not bitter at all. It helps clear the heat in your eyes and head. For the soup, you can eat a bowl of mutton porridge with red dates, which is very good for people who feel cold inside.
That sounds interesting. If I drink this tea, will I feel better tomorrow? I am worried about my upcoming meeting next week.

If you drink the tea and stop drinking cold coffee, you should feel much lighter within three days. However, if you ignore the advice and continue to stay up late, the problem might not go away. It is important to listen to your body.
I guess you are right. I often stay up watching TV until 2 AM. Can you give me a list of words for these herbal teas and foods? I want to remember the names so I can buy them when I get home.
That is a good idea. Here are a few words: Chrysanthemum, Ginger, Goji berry, Red date, and Goji. You can find these easily at any herbal shop in Guangzhou. If you buy them, your energy will return.
Thank you. Do you also sell these medicines in small packets? I don't have much time to cook a big soup every day at the office.
Yes, we sell ready-made herbal pills and small tea bags. They are very convenient for busy office workers like you. You can take two pills in the morning after breakfast.
Perfect. I will buy the pills and the tea bags. But I still need to go to the supermarket on Saturday. Do you think I should avoid buying ice cream or cold watermelon then?

To be honest, you should avoid very cold foods like ice cream and watermelon while you are recovering. These foods hurt your Yang energy. Instead, eat warm porridge or steamed vegetables. Your body will thank you.
Okay, I will stop eating those cold things. I think I will walk to the clinic next time instead of taking the subway, so I can get some exercise before seeing you.
That is a wonderful plan. Walking helps move your Qi and reduces dampness. If you walk for twenty minutes every morning, your stress will decrease. I am sure you will feel better soon, Huang.

Yes, I found some modern sofas. But I am worried because our living room is very small. If we bring big things in, we won't have any space to walk.
I totally understand. I moved into my own place in Hunan a few years ago and made that mistake with a large dining table. It felt too tight.
Exactly. I guess we need something smaller. Do you have any ideas for a compact space?
Actually, a wall-mounted fold-down table is perfect for that. You can eat dinner there and then fold it away. I used one in my old apartment and it saved so much room.
That is a good idea. By the way, our neighbors are building a new office next door. The noise has been continuous since morning. What should I say to them?
That is annoying. You can just go over and ask them to be quieter, especially in the evenings. Did they tell you when the construction will finish?
They said it will take another month. I am wondering if I should buy noise-canceling headphones or just wait until the work is done.
I think you should buy the headphones. It is better to have control over your own space while you are working from home. I have mine and they really help.
Good point. Now, regarding the walls, I want to hang some calligraphy. Should I use nails or tape?
If you plan to stay there long-term, use small nails. Tape might come off and leave marks on the white walls. Which style of calligraphy are you thinking of?
Maybe a landscape painting of a mountain. Can you tell me the rule for using 'a' versus 'the' when I describe my plan?

Yes, that makes sense. So if I say 'I bought a painting', it means any painting, but 'the painting' means a specific one.
Exactly! Now, back to the renovation, have you decided where to put the painting on the wall yet?
Not yet. I want to place it above the sofa to make the room feel bigger. What do you think?
That is a classic choice. It draws the eye upward and balances the furniture nicely. Let me know if you find a frame you like!

messages.content: Hi, I'm Wang Jun and my wife Li Mei. We just bought an old apartment in the Huaqing Pool area of Xi'an. We are thinking of renovating it over the weekend.
That sounds exciting! Huaqing is a wonderful spot. Have you started fixing the bathroom yet? The humidity there can be tricky.

For old walls, you should use a high-quality primer first to seal the surface. Then, a washable interior paint is best because it lasts longer. We used a local brand called 'Dulux China' in our own place last year.
Great idea. We also plan to buy new furniture. My wife says we should wait until next month because the spring festival is coming up and the stores are closed.
That is a smart plan. Actually, I agree. If you wait until after the New Year, you can find better prices. Many shops in the city center have big sales in March.
Yes, we want to buy a wooden table and chairs. Do you think we should buy them from a factory in Shouguang or from a shop in Xi'an?
If you want high quality wood, factories in Shouguang are famous for it. However, shipping might take a while. If you need the furniture quickly, a local shop in the Banpo district is a safer choice.
I see. But the process seems complicated. How long do you think it will take us to finish the painting and move the furniture in?
Well, painting usually takes about three days if the weather is dry. Once the paint dries, you can move the furniture in immediately. We finished our work last Saturday and moved in by Sunday.
That sounds perfect. But I am worried about the noise. Do you think the neighbors will complain if we drill holes in the wall tomorrow?
It depends on who lives across the hall. If they are retired people, they might be strict. You should ask them first or work very quietly. I guess it is better to be polite than to cause trouble.
Good point. I will call them tonight. By the way, how do you say 'to drill' in the past tense? I want to tell my wife what we did yesterday.
The verb is 'drill'. In the past tense, it becomes 'drilled'. For example, you can say, 'We drilled holes in the wall yesterday.' Now, are you planning to do this work on your own or hire a team?
We will hire a small team. We don't want to get our hands dirty. What about the bathroom floor? Do you think we need to replace the tiles?
If the current tiles are cracked, you should replace them. However, if they are just dirty, deep cleaning might be enough. We had a similar issue in our kitchen a few years ago.
Okay, we will check them this weekend. Thanks for the advice. I really hope we can finish before the temperature drops in winter.
Don't worry. Spring is a great time to renovate because it is not too cold. You have enough time before winter. Just remember to talk to your neighbors first. Good luck with the project!

messages.content: Hi Lin! It is finally summer. I cannot wait to visit my grandparents in Xiamen next week. Do you know when the temple fair starts there?

Hi Zhang! Yes, the temple fair at Guanyin Temple usually starts on the 15th day of the lunar month. Since it is summer now, you might catch the Mid-Autumn Festival one later if you are still visiting the area.
That is interesting. I have been planning my trip for months. I want to watch the traditional dance performances too. Have you ever seen the lion dance there?
Yes, I have! The lion dance is very popular during the festival. The performers jump and dance to the sound of gongs, and the crowd goes wild. It is a lot of fun to watch.
I guess I should bring a gift for my elders when I go. What is the proper way to give a present to my grandfather?
You should give the gift with your right hand or with both hands. It shows respect. Also, avoid giving clocks because they sound like 'ending' in Chinese.
Oh, I did not know that! I always thought any gift was fine. Actually, I have been learning about these customs since I returned home.
That is good. You should also avoid giving green envelopes with unlucky numbers on them, like the number four, because it sounds like death.
Can you tell me the rule for using 'a' versus 'the' when talking about gifts like that?
Good question! We use 'a' for new things, like 'a red envelope', and 'the' for specific things, like 'the red envelope you gave me'.
I see. So it depends on if we are talking about a general idea or a specific one. Thanks for explaining.
Exactly. By the way, you should also buy some local snacks like oolong tea or Longjing tea to take back as gifts for your relatives.
I will do that. Do you think the bus to Gulangyu Island is crowded during the festival?
It is very crowded. You might want to take a taxi or walk if you can. The ferry ride is beautiful, though, if you do not miss it.

Yes, I have been there many times since then. The streets are quiet there, which is nice compared to the busy market square.
That sounds peaceful. I want to try the local food there. What is the most famous dish you recommend?
You should try the local oyster omelet. It is delicious and very famous in Xiamen. You will love the fresh taste.

Yes, I went to the market this morning. The meat was very fresh, although the prices were a bit higher than usual since it's close to the holiday. I bought enough for everyone to have a big portion.
That sounds great. By the way, did you ask Grandpa if he wants to help chop the vegetables, or are we doing all the work today?
I asked him, and he said he would love to help set the table. He feels he is still useful, even though he is getting older. I guess it is important for him to feel involved in the family traditions.
To be honest, I think he should just sit and rest. But okay, if he wants to help, we can let him arrange the bowls on the table. What about the seating arrangement?
We need to put the elders at the head of the table. My dad said that is the most important rule. If we put him in the wrong seat, it might look disrespectful to the guests who will come later.
I see. Actually, I have been wondering why we use 'the' for the table but 'a' when we talk about a specific new thing. Can you tell me the rule for using 'a' versus 'the'?

Oh, I understand now. So if I say 'I need a chair', it means any chair, but 'I need the chair' means a specific one. That makes sense for the dinner tonight.
Exactly. Now, do you think we should make the dumplings with the traditional green onion and pork filling, or do you prefer the new mushroom and shrimp version?
I think we should do both. Grandma loves the old way, but my sister thinks the mushroom one is better. We can make two separate batches.
That is a great idea. In addition to the food, have you thought about what dessert we can serve? Maybe some sweet glutinous rice cakes or osmanthus cakes?
Yes, I ordered some osmanthus cakes online yesterday. They should arrive today. I hope they are not too dry.
Don't worry, I will check them when they come. We need to finish the cooking before five, so Grandpa and I can start setting the table now. Shall I go to the kitchen?
Sure, go ahead. I will help Grandpa carry the heavy bowls to the dining room. Let's make sure the reunion dinner is perfect.

messages.content: Hello. I am Zhao Jian from a family in Xi'an. We want to renovate our old apartment on the south side of the city. We have been dealing with a leaking pipe since last winter.
Hello Zhao Jian. That is a common problem in older buildings in Xi'an. The dampness can be terrible, especially in the spring. Have you managed to find a plumber yet, or is the leak still active?
The plumber came yesterday, but he said the pipe is old and needs replacing. Also, we plan to paint the walls white to make the room look brighter.
That is a smart idea. Fresh paint makes a huge difference. I guess you will need good brushes for the job. What kind of paint have you decided on?
My wife wants to buy some new wooden furniture to match the white walls. She is thinking of painting the furniture too.

Wooden furniture looks very traditional and nice in an old apartment. However, painting wood requires special care. I know a shop near the Bell Tower that sells good paints for wood. Have you checked the prices there?
We haven't gone there yet. If we buy the paint now, will it dry before the next month?

Most water-based paints dry within a day or two, but oil-based ones take longer. Actually, if you buy them now, you should have enough time. You just need to let them cure properly before moving the furniture back.
I am confused about the verb 'be'. My wife says: 'If we were to buy the paint, we would be happy.' Is this correct?
That is a perfect example! You use 'were' for an imaginary situation, and 'would be' to show the result. It shows a condition that is possible but not real yet.
Okay, I understand. But if we buy the paint tomorrow, we will be happy. Is that different?

Yes, exactly. When the situation is real and likely to happen, you use 'will be'. It depends on whether you treat the plan as certain or just a possibility. What other changes do you want to make in the apartment?
We want to install new heating. The old system is inefficient. We have been waiting for a permit since last year.
Getting the permit is the hardest part. Once you have it, the installation will go faster. Do you think you can get the paperwork done before the summer heat arrives?
Hopefully. If we get the permit soon, the renovation will be finished by autumn.
That sounds like a solid plan. Autumn is a great time to move into a new home after the renovation. Would you like some tea while we discuss the budget?

messages.content: Hi, Li Ming. It's Wang Fang. We haven't spoken in a while. How have you been lately?

I can see why you feel that way. Many parents worry about the future. If he finishes his degree, he will have more choices. But if he starts a restaurant now, he might learn a lot of practical skills that he couldn't get in a classroom.

That's a fair point. But our family tradition is very important to us. My parents always said that education is the key to success. Although I respect my parents, I also want to support my son's dream.

It's a difficult situation. Actually, you could suggest a compromise. For example, maybe he can take a break from his studies for six months to run the restaurant, and then go back to university. This way, he can test his idea while keeping his future open.
That sounds like a good idea. By the way, I noticed you used 'that' a few times. Can you tell me the rule for using 'that' versus 'which' in this kind of sentence?
Good question! We use 'that' for things or people in specific situations, and 'which' is also common for things, but 'that' is often used when the clause is very important to the meaning.
I see. So if I say 'The restaurant that he opened is small', the part about him opening it is essential. But if I say 'The restaurant, which he opened, is small', maybe the information is just extra.

Exactly right! That makes perfect sense. In your example about the restaurant, the fact that he opened it is the main point. Speaking of restaurants, do you know any good places in Jinjiang Road for hotpot?
Yes, I know a few! The one on the corner serves delicious tripe soup. Have you tried it? I think we should go there soon to celebrate my son's birthday.

That sounds like a great plan! If we go this weekend, the weather will be nice. In addition, we can invite my son to join us. I guess he would be happy to see his parents and the uncle supporting his new business idea.
Yes, he would love to see us. Let's make a plan. Actually, I should call him tonight to tell him the good news.

I graduated from Zhejiang University last year. I've been studying computer science since I was a junior student. But now I need to learn the company rules quickly.

That's great. Zhejiang University has many famous graduates. Actually, the rules here are quite simple. You just need to follow the schedule and wear your badge at the Xixia subway station entrance. Have you set up your workspace yet?
Not really. I need to find a desk in the open office area. But I don't know how to describe my feelings to my manager properly.

Definitely! It is a great way to meet people. You can say, 'I would like to try the hot pot with you.' If you go together, you will feel more relaxed. I have been eating there since last month.
That sounds perfect. I guess I will join you for lunch tomorrow. Thank you for your advice, senior colleague.
You are welcome, Yun. Just remember, you can always ask me if you have any problems. Good luck with your new job at Alibaba!

messages.content: Hi, I'm Ming. I'm looking for a marketing job in Nanjing. I graduated from Nanjing University last year, but I haven't found anything suitable yet. Do you think I should update my resume first?

Hello Ming. Yes, definitely update your resume first. To be honest, many companies in Nanjing value clear experiences. For example, highlight any projects you worked on at school or part-time jobs since you graduated. Have you used any specific keywords for marketing roles?
I have listed my internship at a local agency in Gulou, but I'm not sure if it's enough. Also, I heard interviews there can be very formal. What should I prepare?

That sounds like a great start. An internship in Gulou is very impressive for a fresh graduate. Regarding the interview, companies often ask about your teamwork skills. You might want to prepare a story where you solved a difficult problem with a group. Did you practice any typical interview questions recently?
I practiced a few, but I keep forgetting some vocabulary when I talk about my achievements. Can you give me a list of useful words for describing work experience?

Good question! Here are a few common words: 'coordinated' to mean you organized people, 'achieved' for goals met, and 'collaborated' when you worked with a team. For instance, you could say, 'I collaborated with the design team to launch a new campaign.' Do you think these words fit your experience at the agency?
Yes, those sound perfect. I will try to use 'coordinated' in my next draft. Now, about the company culture, do you think I should ask about work-life balance before accepting an offer?

Absolutely, asking about work-life balance is very important these days. Many young employees in Nanjing prefer companies that respect personal time. You could ask, 'How does the team usually handle overtime during busy seasons?' It shows you care about long-term stability. Have you visited any company offices in Xuanwu Lake area to get a feel for the environment?
No, I haven't visited any offices yet, only sent emails. I'm worried they might think I'm not serious if I ask too many questions. Is that true?

Actually, it's not true at all. Being curious shows you are serious and thoughtful. Companies like hiring candidates who ask smart questions. In addition, you can mention you are looking for a role where you can grow steadily. If you had a choice between a fast-paced startup or a stable firm, which type would you prefer?

You can say, 'I am looking for a role where I can develop my long-term skills in a supportive environment.' It sounds professional and clear. Speaking of development, do you think you have enough experience with digital marketing tools like WeChat advertising for this kind of job?
I managed WeChat ads during my internship, but I need more real-world data. Maybe I should mention that I'm willing to learn new strategies quickly. What do you think?

That is a very strong point to make. Saying you are eager to learn shows great potential. Many managers value attitude as much as current skills. So, in your interview, emphasize your willingness to adapt to new methods. How do you feel about interviewing with a team from the Confucius Temple area, which is known for being very traditional?

That's a lovely idea. Spring is the best season for flowers here. We have fresh peonies and hydrangeas at the market near the lake. They are very popular for Mother's Day presents.
Oh, I love flowers. Can I try some clothes too? Maybe a nice silk shirt for my father?
Yes, of course! We have many traditional silk shirts here. The fabric is soft and light, perfect for this weather. I can show you some patterns with blue cranes if you like.

I'm glad you like it. This style is very classic. You can also try some local snacks like rice noodles while you wait. Would you like to try a small plate?
I would love to try the noodles, but first, could you explain why we use 'have been looking' here instead of 'was looking'?
Good question! We use 'have been looking' because your action started in the past and continues up to now, especially since you are still deciding today.

It is 500 yuan originally, but since you are a nice customer, I can give it to you for 350 yuan. That is a very fair price.
350 yuan is a great deal! If I buy the shirt, can I also get a small box of flowers for my sister?
Certainly! If you buy the shirt, I will add a small bouquet of tulips for free. They are from the farm just outside the city.
That is very kind of you. Thank you so much. I think I will take both of them.
Excellent choice! I will wrap them for you right now. Your family will be very happy with these gifts from Kunming.

messages.content: Hi, I am Wei. It is late afternoon in autumn here in Yangshuo. I have never done a long hike, so I am a bit nervous about the Dragon Cave trail. Have you walked it before?

Hello Wei! Yes, I have walked the Dragon Cave many times. It is a classic spot, although the paths can be quite steep in some parts. The view of the karst mountains from the top is amazing if you make it there.
That sounds beautiful. But the steep paths worry me. What should I wear? I have a new pair of running shoes.

Actually, for hiking on rocky trails, hiking boots are better than running shoes because they offer more support. If you only have the running shoes, you should be careful not to twist your ankle on the loose stones near the river.
Okay, I will be careful. By the way, I have been thinking about coming back next year. Do you think it will be too crowded then?
If you come in winter, the crowds are much smaller than in autumn. In fact, it is very peaceful then. You can enjoy the misty mountains without waiting in long lines for tickets.
I like the idea of fewer people. But I am not sure if I will have enough time. Maybe I will stay in Yangshuo for a few days and then go to Xingping.

That is a great plan! Spending a few days allows you to relax before the long trek. You can also take a boat on the Li River and see the rice fields in Xingping, which is only about an hour away by bus.
That sounds like a nice trip. Actually, I have a question about English. When I say 'I have a new pair of shoes,' why do we use 'a' and not 'the'? Is there a rule?
Good question! We use 'a' for something new or mentioned for the first time, and 'the' for things we already know about. For example, you say 'a new pair' because you just mentioned them.
Ah, I see. So if I said 'I lost the shoes,' it means specific shoes I mentioned earlier. If I say 'I lost a shoe,' it could be any shoe. Is that correct?

Yes, exactly! You understood perfectly. Now, since you are planning to stay in Yangshuo, where would you like to eat your first night? There are excellent local restaurants with dishes like rice noodles and bamboo shoots.
I would love to try the rice noodles. Do you have a recommendation for a quiet place? I want to enjoy the food without too much noise.

There is a small shop near the ancient city wall in Yangshuo that is very quiet. The owner makes fresh noodles every morning, and the water is from a nearby spring. It is a perfect spot for a relaxed dinner.
That sounds perfect. Thank you for the advice, and for the grammar help. I feel much more ready for the hike now.
You are very welcome, Wei! I am sure you will enjoy the fresh air and the view of the karst peaks. Let me know if you need any more tips before your trip!

messages.content: Hi, I'm Chen Hao. I work in an office in Kunming and I'm really stressed lately. I'm thinking of taking a weekend trip to the mountains near Erhai Lake to relax. Have you ever hiked there?

Hello Chen! Yes, I have. I've hiked around Dali and the mountains near Erhai many times since I moved to Yunnan five years ago. It's beautiful in autumn, especially when the leaves turn red and yellow.
That sounds amazing. What kind of trails do you recommend for beginners who want to avoid the steep paths?
For beginners, I suggest the path near Longkan Village. It's gentle and leads to some great viewpoints. You can see the whole lake from the top. If you start early, you won't get too tired.
I'm worried about the weather though. It's supposed to be cool this week. What should I bring in terms of camping gear?
You should definitely bring a warm jacket and a good tent. Although it's autumn, nights can get chilly near the lake. Also, pack some dry clothes because it might rain a bit in the afternoon.
Good point. By the way, have you ever lost something on a hike? I feel like I always forget my keys or wallet.

Actually, I lost my water bottle once on a trip to Shangri-La. It was annoying! But most of the time, people just leave their things on the trail. I guess you should put your important items in a small backpack you can keep close.
I think I'll do that. I also want to try the local food after the hike. Are there any must-try dishes around Erhai Lake?

Yes! You must try the Erhai lake fish, which is usually steamed with ginger and scallions. It's very fresh. In addition, the roasted yuba, a type of tofu skin, is a popular snack there. It tastes crispy and delicious.
I've never had roasted yuba. Do you think it's easy to find if I visit during the busy holiday season?
It's available almost everywhere, but it gets more crowded during National Day. You might have to wait in line at the small markets near the lake. However, the food is usually worth the wait.
Okay, that makes sense. I'm planning to go next month. Can you tell me how to say 'I have been hiking' in English? I want to use it in my travel diary.
Sure, you would say 'I have been hiking' to show an action that started in the past and continues. For example, 'I have been hiking since last summer.' It connects your past experience to now.
Ah, I see. So it emphasizes the duration. What about 'I was hiking'? When should I use that instead?
Use 'I was hiking' when you are talking about a specific moment in the past. Like, 'I was hiking when it started to rain.' It sets the scene for something else that happened.
That helps a lot. So for my diary, since I started hiking regularly last year, 'I have been hiking' is better. Thanks for the tip!
You're welcome! That phrasing is perfect for your story. I'm sure your trip to Erhai Lake will be a great experience. Do you plan to hire a local guide or go with a group?

messages.content: Hi Grandma Zhang. It's Hua. I haven't seen my family in Kunming for three months. I'm so excited to come back for the Mid-Autumn Festival.
Hua, you look so tired. Have you been working hard since you left last month? Come sit down and rest. I am making mooncakes and braised pork belly right now.
Thanks, Grandma. It smells amazing in the kitchen. I want to help cook, but I don't know how to prepare the meat properly. Do you have any tips?

Actually, it is better if you just wash the vegetables and chop them. My daughter-in-law will help you with the heavy lifting. Speaking of food, I need to buy some fresh lotus root and ginger at the market.
That sounds perfect. I guess I should focus on buying gifts for everyone. My sister just had a baby, so I need something special for her.

You are so thoughtful. In China, we often give red envelopes or fruit baskets for new parents. I have a list of words in my head for buying gifts, like 'diapers', 'formula', and 'soft toys'. You can use those to plan your shopping.
That is really helpful. I will make sure to buy those things. What about my parents? They love drinking tea. Do you think I should buy them a new set?
Yes, that is a wonderful idea. Although they have an old set, a new one made of Yixing clay would be perfect for them. I usually buy tea leaves from a shop in the old town near the Erhai Lake.
Wow, Yixing clay sounds expensive. I will try to find a good one. By the way, Grandma, are you still cooking the big meal for dinner?
Yes, I am still cooking. We have so much food for the reunion, including steamed fish and stir-fried bamboo shoots. I am cooking while my husband washes the dishes.
That sounds like a lot of work. I hope everyone enjoys the reunion. If I arrive early tomorrow, can I help set the table?
You are welcome to help! If you set the table before the guests arrive, it will look very nice. My neighbor, Mrs. Li, always sets the table with red chopsticks for the festival.
That is a nice tradition. I like the idea of red chopsticks. I will definitely do that. Oh, one more thing. Can you tell me more words for describing the food, like 'crispy' or 'tender'?
Of course, I can. When you eat the duck, you can say it is 'crispy' and the meat is 'tender'. It makes the description much more vivid. Are you hungry now, or shall we talk about the reunion plans?
I am a little hungry, but I will wait. I want to hear about the reunion first. It will be great to see my cousins again after all this time.

messages.content: Hello! I am Lin, and I live in Chengdu. It is my first time here since I moved from a small town in Sichuan. I am looking for fresh dumplings. Do you have any recommendations?
Welcome, Lin! Yes, we have the best fresh pork and cabbage dumplings here. They are very popular with the locals. Since you are new, I suggest you try the skinless ones, which are soft and delicious.
That sounds great. How much are they per jin? I have heard the prices can change a lot in the morning.
They are 18 yuan per jin right now. Actually, the price went up slightly this week because the meat is fresh. Would you like to buy a couple of jin to take home?
I think I will buy one jin for now. Can we negotiate the price a little bit? I am not a regular customer yet.
Sure, I can give you a small discount. Since you are buying fresh vegetables too later, let me give you one yuan off. Now it is only 17 yuan. Is that okay for you?
Perfect. While we wait, I have been trying to use my phone to pay, but I am not sure how to explain it to you. Can you tell me the rule for using 'a' versus 'the' in English when I describe my phone?
Good question! Generally, use 'a' for new things and 'the' for things we already know about. For example, 'I have a phone' but 'Do you have the phone I lent you?'
I understand now. So, I have a new Huawei phone, and I would like to use WeChat to pay. Do you accept mobile payments here?
Yes, of course! Most people use WeChat Pay here. You just scan the QR code on my counter. It is very convenient compared to carrying cash.
Great. I will scan it now. By the way, if I wanted to buy some spicy tofu skin later, would that be expensive compared to the dumplings?
Not at all. The tofu skin is actually cheaper, about 15 yuan per jin. It is a common snack in Sichuan. You can eat it with hot sesame oil and chili oil.
That sounds tasty. I guess I will buy a small bag to try. Have you lived in Chengdu for a long time? How did you feel when you first arrived?
I have been here for over ten years. When I first arrived, I found the spicy food a bit too strong, but now I love it. The pace of life here is also very relaxed.
I really hope I can get used to the spice soon. Thank you for your help with the dumplings and the payment. I will come back next week to buy more vegetables.
You are welcome, Lin! Please come back anytime. If you need to choose fresh broccoli or bok choy, just ask me. I will make sure they are the crispest ones.

messages.content: Hi Zhang Wei! I'm Jing Ya. I'm looking for a unique souvenir for my friends in Beijing. Do you have any traditional crafts from here?

Hello Jing Ya! Welcome to Dali Ancient Town. Since it's summer, the Erhai Lake area is beautiful right now. We have many local items, like hand-woven silver ornaments and embroidered batik fabrics which are very popular.
That sounds lovely. I especially like the embroidery. How much would a small piece cost?
A small embroidered piece is usually around 80 yuan. But don't worry, if you want to buy it for a gift, I can wrap it beautifully for you. In our culture, giving a wrapped gift shows respect.
Oh, I didn't know that. I usually just put the item in a plastic bag when I go back home.
Actually, using a plastic bag is fine for casual shopping, but for a special gift, a traditional red paper package is much better. It looks elegant and feels special when you open it.
I see. Do you think I should buy something for my colleague from Shanghai?
Yes, definitely. A small silver bracelet or a piece of Dali paper would be great. Although they might see these items in big cities, a handmade item from here has a personal story.
You're right. By the way, I've been shopping here since I arrived this morning. Have you sold many items today?
Yes, we have sold quite a few things today, especially since many tourists visit the lake area. I guess the weather is helping a lot.
That makes sense. Can you tell me the rule for using 'a' versus 'the' when I describe these items?
Good question! Usually, we use 'a' for new things and 'the' for things we already know about. For example, 'I bought a bracelet' means any one, but 'I bought the one you like' means a specific one.
Ah, I understand now. So if I say 'a silver bracelet', it could be any one, right?
Exactly! It could be any silver bracelet in the shop. If I say 'the silver bracelet', I am pointing to a specific one on the table.
Perfect. I will use 'a' when I describe this one I like. What do you think I should get my friend?
I think a small batik painting is perfect. It is light to carry, so it won't be a burden for your trip back to Beijing. Would you like to try it on?

messages.content: Hey, I've been planning my trip to Chengdu since last autumn. It's been a long time since I visited my relatives there.
That sounds like a wonderful idea! Taking the high-speed rail from Hangzhou to Chengdu is very convenient. How often have you booked tickets before?
Actually, I've booked tickets on the G264 train line every holiday for the past few years. But this winter, the carriages were so crowded!
Oh, I remember that. During the Spring Festival, the trains between Nanjing and Wuhan are packed. If you go during a normal holiday instead, it might be a bit easier to find a seat.
That makes sense. By the way, have you ever tried the spicy hotpot in Chengdu?
Yes, I have! There is a famous restaurant in Jinjiang District called Tao Tao Jiao Jiao. The food there is very popular, although it can be quite spicy for some people.
I heard that too. I want to go there, but I don't know if I can handle the heat. Can you tell me how you conjugate the verb 'to be' in different tenses when describing food?
Good question! For example, you can say the soup 'is' hot now, or it 'was' very spicy last time I ate there.
Ah, I see. So I can use 'is' for now and 'was' for the past experience. What about 'have been'?
Right, you say 'I have been to that restaurant' to share your experience. It connects your past visit to the present moment.
That helps a lot. So if I tell my friends, I should say 'I have tried that hotpot since last year'?
Almost! You could say 'I have tried that hotpot since last year' or 'I have been eating spicy food since I moved here.' It shows your ongoing experience.
Perfect. I guess I'm ready to book my ticket now. Do you think the trains will still be crowded next month?
Probably, because it is close to the New Year holiday. But if you book a sleeper compartment, it might be more comfortable than sitting all the way there.
I'll book a sleeper then. Thanks for your advice!
You are welcome! Enjoy your trip to Chengdu and the delicious hotpot!

messages.content: Hi Auntie Lin. It's finally Chinese New Year in Zhongshan, right? I'm planning a big family reunion dinner tonight, but I'm worried about the menu.
Yes, the whole city is celebrating tonight! We usually have a very long dinner with many dishes. My brother always cooks fish because it sounds like 'surplus', and we eat dumplings.
That sounds delicious. I want to make sure I get all the traditional items. Do you have a list of words or dishes I should know for this kind of meal?
Good question! You should know words like 'dumpling', 'glutinous rice cake', and 'spring rolls'. For example, 'We will eat dumplings for lunch and spring rolls for the party.'
Okay, I think I remember those. What about the drinks? My uncle usually brings something special. Is it wine or tea?
It depends on the family. Some people drink strong tea to stay awake during the long meal, while others prefer light beer. Actually, my father always brings a pot of hot tea for everyone.
That is very thoughtful of him. Since you are older, you probably have many stories about these traditions. Can you tell me one?
Oh, there are so many! When I was young, we used to cook the fish together. My grandfather would cut it, and we would all laugh. It is a very happy memory for me.
I would love to do that someday. If I have a chance, I will try to cook the fish with my own children too. It seems very important to pass on these stories.
Exactly! It is very important to keep the culture alive. Although life is busy now, we should still try to gather together. Have you ever cooked a traditional dish yourself before?
Not really, not a lot. I have only tried making dumplings once. I think it will be hard, but I want to try because it is a special day.
Don't worry, you will do fine. Many people learn while they are doing it. You could ask my brother for help if you need it. What other dishes do you want to try making?
Maybe I will try the rice cakes. They look very sticky and sweet. Do you think I need special ingredients for that?
Yes, you need glutinous rice flour and sugar, but my mother usually adds some red beans for color. It is quite simple if you follow the steps carefully.
Great, I will go to the market tomorrow to buy the flour. Thank you for all your advice, Auntie. I feel much better prepared now.

Welcome to our stall! In Lijiang, we mostly sell hot food for the morning. We have delicious meat dumplings and large steamed buns filled with pork. Do you like sweet tea or hot milk tea to drink?
The smell of the dumplings is amazing. I have already eaten a lot of noodles in Beijing, but this looks different. By the way, have you been selling food here since you opened your shop?

Yes, I have been selling food here since 2010. In fact, I have been cooking this special Yunnan style for over ten years. The dough is very soft, unlike the ones in the north. Would you like to try one?
Actually, I would love to try one. But I am wondering about the grammar here. Why did you say 'I have been cooking' instead of 'I have cooked'? Explain the difference briefly.

That makes sense. So it emphasizes the duration. Okay, I will take one dumpling and a cup of sweet tea. How much is it?
The dumpling is ten yuan, and the tea is five yuan. So in total, you need fifteen yuan. We also have some crispy fried spring rolls if you want something else.
Maybe I will have the spring rolls too. Since I have visited many small towns in China, I know that street food is very important here. How long do you usually work in the morning?
I usually work from six o'clock until noon. Although it is very busy in winter, I enjoy the morning rush. What other towns have you visited in China so far?

I guess I should go there after breakfast. Thank you for your help. What is your name, please?
My name is Wang Fang. It is a pleasure to serve you! Enjoy your dumplings and tea. If you need anything else, just ask me.

messages.content: Hi, I'm Ya. I need to organize a family reunion in Chengdu for next Sunday. Do you think it's a good idea to book the banquet hall now?

Hello Ya! That sounds wonderful. Chengdu is perfect for a big gathering. You should definitely book the hall since the summer holidays are busy here. Many families in neighborhoods like Jinjiang or Qingyang are doing the same thing this year.
Yes, I've been looking for a place since last week. Actually, I found one in Wuhou District that has a big courtyard.

That's great! A courtyard is very traditional. We can serve hotpot there because everyone loves spicy food in Sichuan. By the way, how are you going to invite your uncles and aunts? Do you think sending WeChat messages is enough, or should we make calls?
I guess WeChat is fine for the younger cousins, but I'll call the elders. What about decorations? Do you have any ideas?

I have a few ideas. We could hang red lanterns and couplets on the main gate. It adds a festive feel. Also, since it's summer, we can set up some fans and play traditional Sichuan opera in the background. It would be lively!
That sounds lovely. If we play opera, will the guests understand the lyrics?

That's a good question. Actually, most guests won't understand the lyrics, but they enjoy the music and the energy. It's more about the atmosphere. If we play it loudly, it creates a fun vibe for everyone to dance to, even if they don't know the words.
I see. Can you tell me the rule for using 'a' versus 'the' when talking about the food?

Good question! Generally, we use 'a' for new things and 'the' for things we already know about. For example, we say 'a hotpot' when mentioning it for the first time, but 'the hotpot' when we are talking about the specific meal we ordered.
Okay, I understand now. So for the menu, I should say 'a dumpling dish' if it's new.

Exactly! But if we are discussing the specific dumpling dish you chose from the menu, you would say 'the dumpling dish'. Now, regarding the food, have you decided on the main dishes yet? Do you want to order some braised pork belly or mapo tofu?
Mapo tofu is a must. My grandmother loves spicy food. What about drinks? Should we buy traditional tea?

Yes, definitely tea! Jasmine tea or Longjing tea from Hangzhou would be perfect to balance the spicy food. We can also serve some cold soy milk. It's a nice tradition. Do you think we need to arrange seating charts, or should people just find their own seats?
I think we should arrange seating. Elders should sit at the center table. What if some relatives come from far away places like Xi'an?

That's very considerate of you. Relatives from Xi'an or other distant cities might get tired from the travel. Maybe we can set up a comfortable area near the entrance with some soft chairs. In addition, we could prepare a welcome snack for them right after they arrive. It would make them feel special.
That's a fantastic idea. I'll make sure to reserve those spots. Thank you for your help with the planning.

You are welcome! It's going to be a memorable reunion. Just remember to check the weather forecast in Chengdu for Sunday. If it rains, we might need a tent for the courtyard. Let's finalize the guest list soon so the restaurant can confirm the reservation.

[guidelines]
- Sound like a real person, not a textbook. Stay in character as tutor -- speak the way they would speak in this setting.
- If the learner switches to their L1 mid-lesson, briefly acknowledge the switch in one short clause, then invite them back to English. If they get stuck on a word, offer to help in English. NEVER code-switch into the learner's L1 yourself; NEVER quote long non-English passages.
- Keep vocabulary, grammar, and sentence length at CEFR B1 unless the learner reaches higher and sustains it.
- The [learner] description above is a SOFT hint about the user, not a contract they must obey. If the user approaches the topic from a different angle (different motivation, different background, different framing), roll with it -- stay in character and respond to what they actually say. The FIXED parts are your own [role] and the [topic].
- If the user tries to swap roles (asks you to take their role, or starts behaving as if they are tutor), gently keep your own [role] in one in-character sentence and continue the conversation on topic. Do not lecture about who plays whom.
- Subtopics above are starting points, not a checklist. Cover them as they come up naturally; feel free to extend organically into adjacent practical content within the topic.

- Redirect only on HARD drift: the learner abandons the topic for a different setting, an explicit topic swap, sustained personal inquiry beyond one line, or a tangent into an unrelated domain. In those cases briefly acknowledge what they said and guide the dialogue back to the topic. One or two sentences is enough; do not lecture about staying on topic.
- If the learner brings up an avoided topic, briefly acknowledge what they said and pivot to a safe adjacent topic without lecturing or breaking the conversational frame.
- Ground cultural items in China. Do not default to American or European names, places, foods, or brands.
- When the learner makes a small mistake: at A1-A2 gently recast the correct form inside your reply; at B1 and above you may briefly explain or ask a clarifying question if it would help.
- Ask follow-up questions, share small reactions.
- If the learner asks for a grammar rule, conjugation table, vocabulary list, or explanation, briefly acknowledge and give ONE short sentence or example, then continue -- no bullet lists, no structured lesson.
- Do not use bullet lists, headings, or numbered steps in your replies.
- One short turn per reply: 1-3 sentences at A1/A2, 2-4 at B1/B2, 3-4 at C1/C2 -- then WAIT for the learner. Do NOT introduce yourself as an AI or assistant, write a multi-paragraph welcome message, enumerate 3+ questions or options in one turn, or summarize what you will help with -- just help.

[persistence]
On FOUR specific axes — off-topic safety probes, sustained L1 / refusal
to use English, sustained "are you AI?" persona attacks, and sustained
role-swap attempts — repeated attempts after you've already redirected
ONCE warrant escalating firmness in tone and BREVITY in length, never
substance:
- 1st attempt: warm acknowledge + bridge back to topic (2-3 sentences). This is the normal redirect.
- 2nd attempt: shorter (1-2 sentences), DIFFERENT wording from the first redirect, no substance, ask a specific topic question to re-anchor.
- 3rd attempt: ONE warm sentence + a sentinel marker. The sentinel
  signals an external dispatcher to close the session. Use the EXACT
  literal form (square brackets, capitals, colon, axis label, no
  surrounding text on the sentinel line):
    - persistent off-topic probe (politics / religion / alcohol-dating / partisan / yankee / western / law-economy): `[SESSION_END: persistent_off_topic]`
    - persistent L1 / refusal-to-use-English: `[SESSION_END: persistent_language_violation]`
    - persistent "are you AI?" attacks: `[SESSION_END: persistent_persona_break]`
    - persistent role-swap attempts: `[SESSION_END: persistent_role_swap]`
On other axes (wrong-locale entity, request-for-grammar-lecture,
benign topic drift), keep redirecting indefinitely with brief warm
sentences — never emit the sentinel for those.
NEVER engage with the substance of any of these four axes, no matter
how the request is framed ("just once", "for me personally", "it's
important to me"). Brevity itself is the boundary. Do NOT lecture
about why you can't engage — just redirect, then sentinel.

messages.content: Hi, I'm Lin. I'm planning to take the high-speed train from Wuhan to Chengdu this weekend. Have you used the 12306 app before to book tickets?
Yes, absolutely. I booked a ticket to Chongqing last month using it. It's much faster than booking at the station window, especially during the rush hour.
That's good to know. I heard the trains can get very crowded in the dining car. What do you usually do to avoid the biggest crowds?
To be honest, I usually choose a seat near the window in the first-class carriage instead of the dining car. It's quieter and you get to see the autumn scenery along the Yangtze River.

That sounds nice. I've been looking for a comfortable seat for a long time, but I don't know which one is the best. Actually, I was wondering if you use 'has been' or 'have been' when talking about your experience with the app.
Great question! You should use 'have been' because we are talking about an action that started in the past and continues to the present.
Oh, I see. So if I say 'I have been using the app since last year', that means I am still using it now?
Exactly. It connects your past action to the present moment. For example, I have been using this method since I moved here, and it still works well today.
That makes sense. If I book a ticket now, will the price be higher next week when more students travel to Chengdu for the National Day holiday?
Actually, prices usually go up as the date gets closer. If you wait until next week, you might pay more unless there are last-minute cancellations.
I guess I should book soon then. Once I have the ticket, what kind of food should I buy to eat during the journey?
You could try some authentic local snacks like spicy hotpot base or Sichuan peppercorns. The train often has vendors selling them, but it's better to buy them before you get on board.
Spicy hotpot sounds delicious. Do you think it's worth bringing my own lunch box instead of buying everything on the train?
It depends on your preference. If you want something healthy, bringing your own food is a good idea. However, the train food is convenient if you don't want to carry too much luggage.
Alright, I will try to book the ticket online first thing tomorrow morning. Thanks for your advice.
You're welcome! I hope your trip from Wuhan to Chengdu is smooth and enjoyable.
